title: My @Edinburgh Festival Fringe recs for the first half of my trip: @th...
transcript: I am three days into the Edinburgh fringe festival so here are 10 shows that I wholeheartedly recommend these are all shows that I have rated as either four or five stars and they kind of run the gamut from serious dramas to to clowning to a children's puppet show starting with the four star shows first up and one of my highest recommendations is the bengsons Ohio this is one of my most anticipated and I really really loved it the bengsons are both a married couple and a singer songwriter folk group and this show specifically centres around themes of losing your religion but gaining hope and embracing your own mortality both Abigail and Shaun Bengson are disabled and so this show is not only accessible to the audience through things like open captioning through creating a really safe space but it also showcases to the audience the perspective of someone with Shaun’s disability and if you've never heard their music before just go listen to Hundred Days the album right now that's their style and it's the songwriting and lyricism in Ohio is just brilliant I cannot recommend this enough really the only reason that I'm giving it four stars is I don't feel like it fully sticks a landing right now but it could in the future but even in its current state an absolutely fantastic piece of theatre also at four stars I have the late night option Club NVRLAND this is a Peter Pan retelling set in a 2000s Night Club there's a lot of hits from the 2000s if you are a millennial you will know every single song you are encouraged to sing along to dance along it is standing room only if you know the story of Peter Pan you will know what's happening but it follows that story very loosely like again all everybody's human hook is the owner of like a club across the street that competes with Club Neverland Peter Pan is aging and turning 30 at midnight things like that but it's very easy to follow and you're really just there for the vibes and to sing along for something completely different also at Four Stars is Lost Lear at the Traverse Theatre this is a drama about an aging actress who experiences dementia and in her dementia she imagines that she is still rehearsing King Lear as Lear this does a great job of showcasing what the patterns are of someone like dementia it uses puppetry and projections uh it has a really great framing device and at the centre of this to play this aging actress in her prime is an actress in her prime Venetia Bowe who's an incredible force of nature she is so fantastic I would watch her in just a production of King Lear this is another show that is very strong I went back and forth between giving this four or five stars ultimately it drags a little bit in the middle but it it finishes beautifully and even if you aren't familiar with King Lear they do a great job of setting you up with everything you need to know at the top of the show as my final four star show is Lesbian Space Crime which is a hilarious comedy by Airlock Theatre Lesbian Space Crime has three incredible performers telling the story of a lesbian astronaut who is accused of a horrible space crime by her unhinged evil ex wife there are some pretty good songs by fringe standards in it so I would classify it as a musical but the real reason to go see it is the comedy their character work is fantastic the bits that they have and the way that they're able to escalate their humour throughout really keeps you going even when it goes to some ridiculous places beautifully ridiculous places if you are unable to go see lesbian space crime they also have the show Count Dykula here as well which they say is the same thing but with vampires I'm not gonna be able to see that one but it also sounds hilarious so if you see either of those I would recommend both of them on to my 5 star shows starting with alone which is a two person show about these two women on a space mission there's a lot of space in fringe this year stuff is slowly going wrong on this space expedition starting with their slightly clashing personalities and escalating from there this one started off slow but the payoff was so so good and truly some of my favourite design at the fringe so far and I mean like all of the design scenic costume sound lights which is especially impressive because this show literally takes place in like a makeshift box outside of a park because it's Fringe especially if you love science fiction definitely check out alone one of the most harrowing plays that I've seen at the fringe is red like fruit which is another two hander this play features a man and a woman and the woman is a journalist who has been researching a domestic violence case and she is recounting her experience with that article but all of her story is being read aloud by the man and when I tell you this was one of the most emotional shows that I've seen at the fringe so far both performers are doing incredible work on that stage but I was totally drawn in immediately by how gorgeous the writing is by Hannah Muscovitch I was literally sitting there in this that theatre going I I need to own this play immediately and she does such a great job in her playwriting of letting you sit with the material and those who understand what's going on right away get to kind of sit with that and eventually it'll simplify things for the rest of the audience I love that she gives you that chance to do that in the theatre as opposed to spoon feeding you like I feel like a lot of playwrights are tend to do for something completely different a clowning show knight, knight which is one of the funniest things that I've seen this is a one person show performed by Madeleine Rowe who is freaking hilarious and tells the story of King Arthur like you've never seen it before Madeleine has an incredible stage presence and such strong comedic instincts and confidence in their comedic instincts that really makes the audience feel comfortable they also have this incredible ability to read the energy of the room and know how to milk a bit past the point where you're like oh this is going on way too long and then escalates it just enough and pulls the audience back in it was it was incredible to watch and also incredibly entertaining even in all of the silliness and all of the clowning the show itself has fantastic story structure like it takes you on a journey and it it slowly builds you up in the audience to where at first you're like what is happening and by the end you're you're you're in it you're in it you're you've been you've been hooked and if the idea of clowning and audience participation scares you they also do a really great job of getting the consent from all of the audience members so if you do not wanna participate you can just say no and they never feel like you've made the wrong choice next up we have whale where are you going? which is a children's puppet show from Taiwan and is one of the most charming and moving shows that I've seen this week this is truly a show for all ages and I I mean that there was a literal baby in the audience but also like the grandparents were entertained and even though the entire thing is wordless there is a story in there of this old man who has had this event happened in his past that he's kind of locked away and then through some magical means a boy appears in his life that kind of opens him up just absolutely charming the performances were incredible the puppets were so cute and the kids in the audience were just entranced and for a lot of them it was probably their first show and I was in the audience just crying I it it made me emotional I cannot recommend it enough even if you don't have a kid go see it and saving the best for last my top two picks that I cannot recommend enough Are don't tell dad about Diana which is an absolutely charming and hilarious story about these two Irish friends who are participating in a drag competition and preparing a Diana inspired drag competition in the late 90s it is a beautiful coming of age story both of the performers are incredible the writing is so funny and again the the way that the show is paced is wonderful and it's one of those comedies that even when you figure out where the scene is going it still takes you on such a fun ride and finally my favourite show so far and one that may also be one of my top picks of the year if we're being honest is she's behind you she's behind you is a one person show told by Johnny Mcknight who is a premier Scottish dame in pantos if you don't know what pantos are don't worry because he explains it all to you but one thing about pantos is that they follow very specific rules they have a lot of roots in commedia dell'arte so they use stock characters there's specifics for where characters can enter from calls and responses with the audience every show ends with a wedding but there's also a lot of outdated aspects of panto and so Johnny Mcknight takes you through not only his history with the art form but the rules that he's created for moving the art form forward and how ultimately playing a dame helped him become a better man I cannot recommend this enough I very much put it in the same vein as of my son's a queer where I think she's behind you is the kind of theatre that I just think makes the world a better place it is both hilarious and inspirational and will make you believe that theatre can in fact change the world which I already believe those are my recs so far please drop yours in the comments I still have a couple slots open
